transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-09-17
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (BlueHarbor Platform Lead), Jonah (BlueHarbor FinOps), Ibrahim (BlueHarbor SRE)

--- Auto summary (short) ---
Quick console tour focused on per-route economics and pilot scoping; discussed KV/prefix cache, batching, quantization tradeoffs, and private deployment cost considerations. Next: pricing + pilot config to be sent.

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, um thanks for hopping on. I'm Samira, account exec for Redwood. Today Ethan and I will walk through the Console route-level views and the cost map. Maya, Jonah, Ibrahim, thanks for doing this.
00:18 Maya: thanks, quick note we mostly care about mapping inference spend back to product routes and being able to set alerts when cost per route deviates.
00:32 Ethan: perfect, we'll start in the Routes tab. you'll see we've grouped by route tag, you can also roll up by service, environment, or customer id. Notice the token-level column — that's where we break down prompt vs completion tokens and the implied cost.
00:54 Jonah: is that a derived cost from model selection + infra or do you pull billing from our cloud?
01:05 Ethan: it's derived from the model footprint and the runtime profile — so we take per-token model compute cost, plus an amortized GPU runtime overhead. if you're on Redwood Dedicated or Private, you can input your committed capacity and we compute effective unit costs. there is also an option to reconcile with your cloud billing export for cross-check.
01:28 Maya: okay, can we tag routes automatically? we have multiple teams and routes proliferating.
01:35 Samira: yeah you can push tags via the SDK or the route registry API. we also support heuristics — if a route path matches certain patterns we auto-suggest tags in the console.
01:50 Ibrahim: how does caching show up? we have a few short prompt routes that could be cached at prefix-level but we worry about staleness.
02:04 Ethan: good question. in the Route Insights panel you'll see cache hit rate, average saved tokens, and estimated cost saved per hour. note the UI labels it as "kayvee cache" in some transcriptions if you export, weird quirk — but the data is correct. we show prefix/KV caching separately from full-response caching. prefix cache is safe for stateless prompts and yields large token savings.
02:32 Jonah: is there a back-of-envelope for when cache is worth it? eg, if cache hit rate > 10% and average saved tokens > 40 then it's worth enabling?
02:44 Ethan: exactly, we surface a recommendation card. for small prompts the break-even is lower because startup overhead is minimal. We'll also simulate cost impact when you toggle caching on the route.
03:01 Maya: what about batching? some of our flows are synchronous user-facing, others are async.
03:10 Ethan: the console shows histogram of latency vs batch size; for latency-sensitive routes we suggest small batch sizes and KV cache, for throughput you can increase batch windows. also our Optimize tool will propose batching profiles per route and you can preview estimated latency and cost after applying.
03:27 Jonah: can we see unit economics per persona? like map cost to a customer account?
03:35 Samira: yes, route metadata supports customer_id and product_segment. you can pivot dashboards to show spend per customer or top-N customers by cost. we also have alerting so you can be notified on cost anomalies.
03:48 Ibrahim: about private deployment — how does the cost model change if we run Redwood Private in our VPC? we have strict egress + KMS rules.
03:58 Ethan: for Private we give two models: appliance + support fee or license + usage. you supply your GPU fleet and we run the control plane privately. cost reporting still works — you feed telemetry to the console over secure peering. KMS/HSM integrations supported; encryption-at-rest and audit log forwarding for SOC2/ISO audits.
04:20 Maya: do you have SOC2 Type II evidence and pen test reports? procurement will need those.
04:28 Samira: yes — I'll attach the security pack in the follow-up. we also have an NDA-friendly summary for sensitive customers.
04:36 Jonah: we run cost forecasting on a monthly cadence. can the console project spend if we change model variants or enable 4-bit quantization?
04:47 Ethan: yeah, under Model Switch you can simulate shifting a route from a 8-bit to 4-bit quantized variant or change the model family. it recomputes estimated compute cost and shows projected latency shifts. small note: quantization can change output distributions slightly; we recommend eval runs with your prompt set and Redwood Optimize will flag quality regressions.
05:12 Maya: hmm that eval step is important for us. can you hook evals to the rollout? we want automatic rollback if quality drops.
05:21 Ethan: absolutely — our rollout policies support canary traffic, A/B, and auto-fallback on quality metrics or latency SLO breaches. you define the eval suite in the console or upload your test set.
05:33 Samira: let's jump into an example route — Ethan, can you open the "signup_nudge" route?
05:39 Ethan: sure — opening. okay, this route is 12% of total tokens, high completion tokens due to long form responses. see the cost burn down by day, and this little panel shows top prompts and conversion metric ties if you send product metrics back via the telemetry SDK.
06:02 Jonah: conversion tie-in is huge. does that require custom instrumentation?
06:08 Ethan: minimal — the SDK can attach metric labels. we also provide a small sidecar that maps request ids to product events so you can compute cost per conversion.
06:18 Maya: the UI is helpful but we need CSV exports for finance.
06:22 Samira: export button in top-right, you can schedule daily exports or push to S3/BigQuery.
06:28 Ibrahim: any gotchas with token counting? we've seen different tokenizers behave differently and that screws up forecasts.
06:36 Ethan: we use model-specific tokenizers and tag token counts with model name and tokenizer version. still some customers upload their own tokenizer for legacy reasons — console handles that mapping.
06:48 Jonah: what about spikes — if a route suddenly doubles, do you have automated fallback to a cheaper model?
06:55 Ethan: yes, routing policies can failover to a cheaper compatible variant or to a lower-quality quantized family. we also have regional fallbacks. all of this is visible in the traffic flow simulator in the Console, so you can run a "what-if" for spikes.
07:15 Maya: can we run a short pilot — say 3 routes for 4 weeks? we want to validate cost savings and monitor quality.
07:23 Samira: that's exactly what a sandbox pilot is for. we'll scope a pilot that includes: console access, routing policy templates, Redwood Optimize recommendations, one weekly checkpoint with an SE, and a final report with cost delta and quality metrics.
07:38 Jonah: pricing on pilot?
07:41 Samira: pilots are usually credit-backed; we'll send a pilot agreement. post-pilot pricing depends on committed capacity or usage; I'll outline both.
07:50 Ibrahim: any limitations on on-prem GPUs? we run mix of A100 and older V100s.
07:57 Ethan: runtime will auto-select kernels but older GPUs may have slower per-token throughput; we recommend a small benchmark run which I can run with your image. I'll drop the benchmark harness.
08:12 Maya: great. can you show alerts definition?
08:16 Ethan: sure — quick demo: create alert -> scope to route tag -> metric = cost-per-hour or token-cost-per-request -> condition > baseline * 1.5 for 10 minutes -> notify to Slack/email or webhook to your incident management.
08:36 Jonah: perfect. ok last Q — can we integrate the console with our internal billing so we can automatically reconcile?
08:44 Samira: yes, we support exporting aggregated usage to your billing pipeline or you can pull raw events via the telemetry API.
08:52 Maya: thanks, this feels promising. what I want after this call is the pricing + the benchmark template + sample alert rules.
08:59 Samira: noted, we'll send those. Ethan will follow up on the benchmark and cache configs.
09:05 Ethan: I'll also include suggested quantization profiles per model family given your latency targets.
09:12 Jonah: cool. timeline — can we kick off pilot next Monday?
09:16 Samira: I'll propose a slot in the follow-up, if BlueHarbor completes the route list and telemetry access by Friday we can.
09:23 Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
09:27 Ibrahim: thanks.
09:29 Samira: bye all.

--- End transcript ---
